checked.claim: A GM's Remnant card keeps an author pick the GM cancelled when a watched event redraws the card while 'Who left this Remnant' is open.
checked.why: Read the whole road. The card is a keepLive region watching every item and token hook and remnantStore, with no whileEditing (grep: no whileEditing anywhere in scripts/). The author select has no name, id or data-drpg-key, so it is keyed by position; it is drawn with the stored author selected (authorOptions), so after the GM's pick isDirty is true and capture carries the pick, restore writes it onto the new select. Both focus roads end the same: if the question takes focus, isEditing is false and the redraw runs 120 ms after the event; if focus stays on the select, the event leaves pending and the focusout of the pointerdown on Cancel forces rebuild(true) before Cancel's click resolves. Either way Cancel then writes 'was' onto the detached old select, and the new select shows the unsaved pick with no change event left. A redraw of the trace's own sheet (renderActorSheetV2 -> body.innerHTML) would draw the stored author afresh, but only an update of that token's actor does that, not another token's move. No test pins the cancel road (grep authorReplace / data-drpg-author in scripts/tests*.mjs: one source-shape test, tests-tier1.mjs:8879). Severity raised: the card states a saved author the ledger does not hold, which Observe's Follow My Traces, an incident's tie and Tamper read - wrong in a particular situation (11.3 minor), not dirt or text.

checked.claim: On a reshape card whose Remnant is gone, Approve answers null, the card stays open, and each further press whispers the roller 'already gone' again; Refuse then says the Remnant 'reads as before'.
checked.why: applyReshapeRuling returns null on !data before the claim is used (claim is computed only when data exists), so no 'ruled' mark is written and a second press is ruled again. askReshapeRuling passes the null through (res.value?.value ?? null); ruleApproveReshape settles only on false or truthy; claimCard drops the card's claim when the outcome is neither settled nor held, and wireCallActions releases the buttons. A reset of the 'incident' group drops the attempt row, but that changes only Refuse (claimRuling then answers value false and the card settles as voided), not Approve, which returns null on !data first. Refuse with the row standing: claimRuling succeeds, the erase branch finds no token, and 'said' stays DRPG.Cleanup.reshapeDeclined. No test pins the gone road (grep reshapeRulingGone in scripts/tests*.mjs: only a key-list check, tests-tier0.mjs:5225). Severity kept: the GM has Refuse as a way out and is told the player was informed; the cost is a repeated whisper and a wrong line in an uncommon situation. The verdict label 'stale-state' fits a flow defect better than a redraw one, which does not change the finding.
